response.rationale: I think these are two different concepts, though the evidence is limited. A (ClubBooking) has its own store: ClubBookingRepository (node 440da90bcde7901a) keeps `private readonly bookings = new Map<string, ClubBooking>();` in src/persistence/clubBookingRepository.ts. Its callers are ClubBookingService, which has create, get, list and invoice methods, and SessionService.effectiveCapacity. That suggests a club booking is invoiced and holds capacity on a session, likely as a block reservation. B (Booking) comes from a different store: ReportService (node a663bd12cbc0090c) gets it through BookingRepository.findBySession and checks `if (b.status === "paid") {` in src/business/reportService.ts, so a booking has its own payment status. Separate repositories, services and lifecycles (invoicing for one, a paid status for the other) point to separate business concepts. The shared word "booking" isn't enough to treat them as one.
